text: 🇲🇽✊ "They turned rights into privileges. We recovered the essence that the people have rights." "We consider housing, education, health, and the pension for older adults a right of the people of Mexico — and we are advancing in access to those rights." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on housing as a right Her housing report: about 12 million families reached, 667,000 homes contracted, 277,000 under construction. Health centers that once charged fees are now free.
banner: HOUSING: A RIGHT, NOT A PRIVILEGE

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "When a people knows its strength and its history, there is nothing that can stop it." "In 1990, 58% of Mexicans felt proud to be Mexican; today it is 90%. That was not given to Mexico by neoliberalism — it was given by the Fourth Transformation." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on national dignity She cited an El Financiero poll on national pride. It is Independence week in Mexico — the Grito is September 15.

🚨🇲🇽 "We are neither a piñata nor a matter for the Americans." "The U.S. election — let them settle it over there. Mexico has no reason to be a factor in it. We collaborate, we coordinate, but the U.S. vote is defined by the problems of the United States." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on US intervention claims She was rebutting a US-sourced narrative that Mexicans want a foreign operation against the cartels. She cited polling: only about 9% back a US operation on Mexican soil; roughly 91% oppose any foreign intervention.

🇲🇽🎨 "Public education is the same for the landowner as for the field hand." "Our obligation is for the public school to be the best — and it already is, even better than private. Adjusting for socioeconomic level, public schools scored better than private ones." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on education On the PISA results: she credits the teaching corps vilified during the neoliberal education reform, and notes the test recognizes Mexico's reduced educational inequality.

🇲🇽✊ "GDP grew 1% under López Obrador — and 13.5 million families rose out of poverty." "The problem isn't only growth, but the distribution of wealth: wages, well-being programs and public works distribute it. That's why we must speak of development, not just growth." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on development vs growth Rebutting analysts fixated on GDP figures; she frames wages, well-being programs and public investment as the mechanism that distributes the gains.

🏠🇲🇽 "Gentrification is displacing those who originally lived in a place." "...so people of another economic level move in, with housing priced so only a small percentage can afford it. Some governments drive it with corruption, like the Benito Juárez real-estate cartel that violated land-use rules through officials' bribes." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on gentrification On foreigners earning in dollars and spending in pesos displacing residents in Mexico City, Guadalajara, Tijuana and the Riviera Maya. Her answer: the state builds social housing to pull private prices down.

🔥🇲🇽 "They are not information media, they are propaganda media." "Many outlets in Mexico have one objective: to be propaganda for the right. They have a group chat where they agree on what they'll all say that week. Their objective is to return to the past of corruption and privilege." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the press Responding to columnists dismissing Mexico's internal-market-driven growth and to the week's coordinated attack lines.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>A Record July: 4.41 Million Tourists Chose Mexico</u>

Mexico drew 4.41 million international tourists in July, up 3.8% year-on-year and a record for the month, per INEGI's traveler survey — total international visitors reached 8.65 million (+2.9%), with border tourism surging 13.2%. The country the US State Department keeps slapping with travel warnings just posted its busiest July on record.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>The Country That Believes in Trains Again</u>

Mexico will open the AIFA–Pachuca passenger train in 2027, a 58-km line built to move over 100,000 riders a day at 120 km/h, President Sheinbaum confirmed — part of a public rail revival that also includes the México–Querétaro and Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo routes. Forty years after the neoliberals scrapped passenger rail and sold off the tracks, the state is laying them back down.
